extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners and patent practitioners (applicants/agents/attorneys) involved in claiming foreign priority and incorporation-by-reference issues
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on claiming and perfecting foreign priority (37 CFR 1.55 etc.) and on incorporating omitted specification/drawings by reference (37 CFR 1.57(b)), including examiner procedures, timing, documentation, translations, post-issuance remedies, and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation location for foreign priority claim (date-dependent)
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications filed on or after September 16, 2012, the claim for foreign priority must be presented in an application data sheet (37 CFR 1.76(b)(6)). For applications filed prior to September 16, 2012, the priority claim is presented in the oath or declaration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the priority claim is placed in the correct document depending on filing date; this affects whether additional oaths/declarations are needed and may impact procedures for later corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notation of U.S. application data on foreign priority papers (best practice)
rubrics_metrics.description: It is suggested that a notation of the application number of the corresponding U.S. application be placed on the priority papers when such papers are not submitted via a priority document exchange program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place the notation directly on the priority papers themselves (not just on a cover letter) because cover letters and priority papers can become separated; doing so substantially lessens correlation problems between priority papers and the U.S. application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner's initial review of submitted priority papers
rubrics_metrics.description: When a claim to priority and the certified copy of the foreign application are received while the application is pending, the examiner generally makes no examination of the papers except to see that they contain no obvious formal defects and correspond in number, date, and country to the application data sheet, oath/declaration, or application data sheet for later filings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For original applications under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) (other than design) and international applications entering national stage under 35 U.S.C. 371, the examiner should ensure the foreign priority claim is timely. Examiners may use form paragraph 2.21.01 to notify applicant that the foreign priority claim is untimely. See MPEP § 214.03.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to examine entitlement to priority (intervening references / AIA FITF context)
rubrics_metrics.description: The subject matter of the application is not examined to determine entitlement to the priority of the foreign filing date unless such determination is required for patentability reasons (e.g., when an intervening reference by the inventive entity is found with an effective date between the foreign filing date and the U.S. filing date under the AIA FITF provisions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an intervening reference is found, examiner may reject claims as unpatentable without paying attention to priority date if certified copy not yet filed. Applicant may argue or file foreign papers to overcome rejection. Examiner may require foreign papers (and repeat or continue the rejection as appropriate). Form paragraph 2.19 may be used (Overcome Rejection by Translation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation requirement for non-English certified copy
rubrics_metrics.description: When an English language translation of a non-English language foreign application is required, the translation must be that of the certified copy (of the foreign application as filed) submitted together with a statement that the translation of the certified copy is accurate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant files the certified copy to overcome an intervening reference, the translation should be required at the same time. Examiner may reject unpatentable claims and require an English translation if the certified copy is not in English and no translation is present. See 37 CFR 1.55 and MPEP §§ 215 and 216.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner action after certified copy and translation are filed
rubrics_metrics.description: If the certified copy and translation (if necessary) are filed to overcome the date of a reference, the examiner is to study the certified copy (and translation) to determine if the applicant is entitled to the priority date. If entitled, the rejection is withdrawn; if not entitled, repeat the rejection stating reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If certified copy is already in file when an intervening reference is found, study it; if entitlement is shown, do not rely on the reference (may cite to applicant on form PTO-892); if not, reject unpatentable claims with explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certified copy inventor/applicant name consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: If the nonprovisional application and the certified copy of the foreign application do not name the same inventor or do not have at least one joint inventor in common, the priority date should be refused until the inconsistency is resolved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If certified copy corresponds with the one identified in ADS or oath/declaration and no discrepancies appear, entitlement may be assumed; otherwise require resolution per MPEP § 213.02.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examine foreign application for identity of invention and sufficiency under 35 U.S.C. 112
rubrics_metrics.description: The most important aspect of the examiner’s action pertaining to a right of priority is the determination of the identity of invention between the U.S. and the foreign applications. The foreign application must be examined for sufficiency of the disclosure under 35 U.S.C. 112 as well as to determine if there is a basis for the claims sought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A nonprovisional application may be entitled to the filing date of the foreign application for some claims and not others; applicant may rely on multiple foreign applications for different claims. For UK provisional specifications, note that they need not contain a complete disclosure under 35 U.S.C. 112; if insufficient, reliance may be had on a complete specification if presented, which would be treated as a different application.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 119(b)(1) identification requirements for priority
rubrics_metrics.description: No application for patent shall be entitled to this right of priority unless a claim is filed identifying the foreign application by specifying the application number on that foreign application, the intellectual property authority or country in or for which the application was filed, and the date of filing the application, at such time during the pendency of the application as required by the Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Director may consider failure to file a timely claim as a waiver and may establish procedures (including fees) to accept unintentionally delayed claims; Director may require certified copy, translation, and other information (certified by foreign authority) showing dates of application and specification filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to accept delayed priority claim under 37 CFR 1.55(e) — required contents
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition to accept a delayed claim for priority under 35 U.S.C. 119(a)-(d) or (f) must be accompanied by: (1) the priority claim in an application data sheet identifying the foreign application by application number, country, and filing date; (2) a certified copy of the foreign application (unless previously submitted or an exception applies); (3) the petition fee (§ 1.17(m)); and (4) a statement that the entire delay was unintentional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director may require additional information where there is a question whether the delay was unintentional. See 37 CFR 1.55(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limits for filing certified copy of foreign application (37 CFR 1.55(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: For an application under 35 U.S.C. 111(a), a certified copy must be filed within the later of four months from the actual filing date of the application, or sixteen months from the filing date of the prior foreign application, in an original application under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) filed on or after March 16, 2013 (except design applications). For an international application entering the national stage under 35 U.S.C. 371, the certified copy must be filed within the PCT time limits or within the later of four months from national stage commencement or sixteen months from the prior foreign filing date, subject to exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a certified copy is not filed within the specified period and no exception applies, the certified copy must be accompanied by a petition showing good and sufficient cause and the petition fee (§ 1.17(g)). See paragraphs (h),(i),(j) for exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: General requirement to file priority claim, certified copy, and translation during pendency (37 CFR 1.55(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim for priority and the certified copy of the foreign application must, in any event, be filed within the pendency of the application, unless filed with an appropriate petition under 37 CFR 1.55(e) or (f) (or with fee and showing of good and sufficient cause under (g)). If the claim or certified copy is filed after payment of the issue fee, the patent will not include the priority claim unless corrected by a certificate of correction under 35 U.S.C. 255 and § 1.323.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to perfect a claim before issuance may be cured via certificate of correction or reissue, subject to the constraints discussed (e.g., whether further examination would be required). See MPEP § 214.02.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perfecting a priority claim via certificate of correction (conditions)
rubrics_metrics.description: A certificate of correction under 35 U.S.C. 255 and 37 CFR 1.323 may be requested and issued to perfect a claim for foreign priority benefit in a patent if: (1) the requirements of 35 U.S.C. 119(a)-(d) or (f) had been satisfied in the patented application or in a parent application prior to issuance of the patent; (2) the requirements of 37 CFR 1.55 are met; and (3) the correction sought would not require further examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where priority claim was timely filed but certified copy requirement not satisfied, a certificate of correction accompanied by a grantable petition under 37 CFR 1.55(f) (or (g) for design) may be used. A petition under 37 CFR 1.55(e) to accept an unintentionally delayed claim is not needed in that scenario.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perfecting a priority claim via reissue (when certificate not appropriate)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the requirements for certificate of correction are not met, or if the correction sought would require further examination (e.g., where foreign application has a pre-March 16, 2013 filing date in a patent examined under FITF), the claim to foreign priority benefits can be perfected only by way of a reissue application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.55(h) also provides that the certified copy requirement will be considered satisfied if a prior-filed nonprovisional application for which benefit is claimed contains a certified copy of the foreign application and is identified as containing that certified copy. Case law (e.g., Brenner v. State of Israel; In re Van Esdonk) illustrates circumstances where reissue or parent application perfection can satisfy requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation by reference relief under 37 CFR 1.57(b) — threshold rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to conditions and requirements, if all or a portion of the specification or drawings is inadvertently omitted from an application, but the application contains a claim under 37 CFR 1.55 or 1.78 that was present on the filing date, and the inadvertently omitted portion is completely contained in the prior-filed application, the claim under 37 CFR 1.55 or 1.78 shall be considered an incorporation by reference of the prior-filed application as to the omitted portion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.57(b) provides a safeguard for inadvertent omissions allowing later amendment to add omitted material if it is completely contained in a prior-filed application; see also MPEP § 608.01(p) for explicit incorporation statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions and requirements to add omitted material under 37 CFR 1.57(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: To add omitted material pursuant to 37 CFR 1.57(b) the following must be met: (A) the application must have been filed on or after September 21, 2004; (B) the material must have been inadvertently omitted; (C) a claim under 37 CFR 1.55 (priority) or 1.78 (benefit) must have been present on the filing date; (D) the omitted portion must be completely contained in the prior-filed application; (E) applicant must file an amendment to include the omitted portion within any Office-set time but no later than close of prosecution (37 CFR 1.114(b)) or abandonment; (F) if not otherwise entitled to a filing date, petition under 37 CFR 1.53(e) with fee; (G) applicant must supply a copy of the prior-filed application (except where prior-filed application is under 35 U.S.C. 111); (H) supply an English translation if prior-filed application is not in English; and (I) identify where the omitted portion can be found in the prior-filed application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ‘Completely contained’ requires express (not implicit) disclosure in the prior-filed application as filed. No separate declaration of inadvertence is required—filing the amendment constitutes a certification under 37 CFR 11.18(b) that the omission was inadvertent (Office may inquire if record raises issue). Amendments must comply with 37 CFR 1.57(b) and 1.121. Amendments submitted in reply to a final Office action which first raises the omitted material issue are treated under 37 CFR 1.116 (no right of entry). If prosecution closed or application abandoned, applicant may file RCE (37 CFR 1.114) or petitions (37 CFR 1.137) as appropriate. If application is patented, certificate of correction or reissue cannot be used to add omitted material via 1.57(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical timing and procedural examples for 37 CFR 1.57(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: If OPAP mails a ‘Notice of Omitted Item(s)’, applicant should submit an amendment under 37 CFR 1.57(b) within the two-month time period set in the notice and identify it as such. Any amendment to an international application pursuant to 1.57(b)(1) will be effective only as to the United States and will not affect the international filing date; to add omitted material after prosecution is closed, applicant must reopen prosecution (e.g., by filing an RCE) and submit an amendment compliant with 1.57(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: (1) OPAP noticed omission of a figure and provided two-month reply period; applicant may rely on 1.57(b) but must file amendment in compliance with 1.57(b). (2) For international applications, 1.57(b) relief cannot alter international filing date or make an international application entitled to a filing date under PCT Article 11; any addition for effect in all designated states must follow PCT rules (PCT Rule 20).
